messages:
nina: quick flag — API ref shows `timeout=1000` for /v1/run examples. our server interprets timeout as seconds, not milliseconds. customers are setting 1000 and their requests fail immediately with 504.

omar: oof. where exactly? openapi examples or the quickstart snippets?

nina: both. openapi/paths/run.yaml example query uses `?timeout=1000`, and the curl/python/js snippets copy that. support reported at least two customers this week.

support: collected a repro: curl -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/run?timeout=1000' returns 504 after short default window; changing to `?timeout=1000s` or `?timeout=1` (seconds) behaves as expected.

omar: plan: update OpenAPI param description to explicitly state "integer seconds", change examples to `?timeout=1` (for one second) and `?timeout=30` for 30s. update generated SDK snippets to be explicit about units.

nina: for JS snippet, instead of `timeout: 1000`, show `// SDK expects seconds; convert to ms for fetch` plus code `const seconds = 30; const timeoutMs = seconds * 1000; fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs) })`. add a short inline comment about the mismatch.

omar: good call. for server-side examples (curl/python) keep seconds in querystring. for client-side SDK examples, include explicit conversion. I'll make the PR updating openapi, examples, and snippets; also add a one-line migration note: "timeout is expressed in seconds in the API; if your code passed milliseconds, divide by 1000 or update callers."

nina: can we also add a small doc-test that runs examples through a mock server to verify units? we've had unit mismatches slip through before.

omar: yes adding tools/docs/validate_examples to assert param types and a specific rule for duration-like params (ensure example values are plausible).

omar: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4512 — updates openapi/paths/run.yaml, snippets/run_examples.{js,py}, and adds migration note + docs CI test.

docs-bot: docs-ci started for PR 4512 (:building_construction:)

nina: small nit: in the python snippet use `requests` with timeout in seconds (`requests.post(..., timeout=30)`) — don't convert to ms there. make sure examples are idiomatic per language.

omar: done. updated python to `timeout=30` and left JS conversion comment. pushed.

docs-bot: docs-ci passed for PR 4512 (:white_check_mark:) — https://ci.internal.redwood/4512

support: confirmed resolved for customer case #20789 after docs update.

omar: merged and cherry-picked to `stable/docs` branch. added changelog entry: "docs: clarify timeout units in /v1/run examples (seconds, not ms)"

nina: thanks! that should stop more confusing 504s.

omar: thanks all — follow-up: I'll open a tiny issue to scan for other duration-like params (poll_interval, wait_timeout) to ensure consistency across the API reference.
